# Fake quote set

Thirteen fictional supplier quotes used for development, demos and the Phase 5 scenario tests. Nine of them form three scored scenarios with deliberate traps; four more cover edge cases. Every company, address, phone number and GST number is made up, and each file is marked "SAMPLE - FICTIONAL". No real company data is used.

The expected results are in the [answer key](answer-key.md) ([JSON](answer-key.json)).

## Scenarios

| Scenario | Buyer (fictional) | Buyer GST | Quotes and formats | Main traps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A: clinic supplies | Bukit Fern Family Clinic | Not registered | A1, A2, A3: three text PDFs with different layouts | Boxes of 100 vs single pieces; a wrong line total |
| B: cafe ingredients | Kopi Lantern Cafe | Registered | B1 text PDF, B2 phone photo (JPG), B3 Excel | 5-cent rounding; a supplier with no GST; a delivery fee at the bottom of the sheet |
| C: construction materials | Tembusu Build & Renovation Pte Ltd | Registered | C1 text PDF, C2 text PDF in USD, C3 scanned PDF | Bags, tons and kg; USD prices; GST that leaves out delivery |

## How the files are made

The files are generated by [`tools/fake-quotes`](../../tools/fake-quotes). The quote contents, including every deliberate mistake, are written out in `quotes.py` exactly as a supplier would print them; the generator only lays them out. Scans and the photo are made by rendering the PDF to an image and adding tilt, grain, blur and JPEG compression, so OCR has something realistic to read.

To regenerate (from the repo root, on Windows):

```
python -m venv tools/fake-quotes/.venv
tools/fake-quotes/.venv/Scripts/pip install -r tools/fake-quotes/requirements.txt
tools/fake-quotes/.venv/Scripts/python tools/fake-quotes/generate.py
```

If a quote's contents change, the answer key must be worked out and checked by hand again.

## Rules

- Only fictional data goes in this folder. Postal codes are `0000xx`, phone numbers `000-000x`, GST numbers `FAKE-GST-xxxx` and email domains `.example`.
- The answer key is the reference for the scenario tests. It is checked by hand, not produced by the app.
